comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded Processor and GPU Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers embedded CPUs, APUs, and GPUs, including EPYC Embedded, Ryzen Embedded V/R-Series, and Radeon Embedded products, designed for high-performance compute, networking, storage, and graphics in enterprise and automotive markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD explicitly identify in-vehicle infotainment and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) as key automotive drivers for their respective embedded product portfolios. MU highlights that automotive memory products enable advanced infotainment with larger displays and support ADAS vision/sensor systems, while AMD’s embedded GPUs and processors are designed to meet the high-performance 3D graphics and 4K multimedia requirements of automotive infotainment, alongside high-performance compute for these systems.

sentences.text: Automotive memory and storage products enable connected, advanced infotainment systems with increasingly larger and higher definition displays and support improved voice and gesture control.
Our products enable increasingly advanced vision and sensor based automated systems to support driver assistance solutions and vehicle safety.

Our embedded processors and GPUs are designed to support high performance compute, high-bandwidth network connectivity and security, high-performance storage requirements for enterprise and cloud infrastructure, 3D graphics performance and 4K multimedia requirements of automotive infotainment systems.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom provides products for factory automation, renewable energy, and automotive markets, including optocouplers, sensors, and Ethernet ICs used in EV powertrains and driver assistance systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose serving the automotive market with specific technologies for ADAS and infotainment. Broadcom (AVGO) lists Ethernet ICs and sensors as products used in vehicle subsystems including advanced driver assistance systems, whereas Micron (MU) focuses on high-performing memory and storage products qualified for these same intelligent automotive services and ADAS capabilities.

sentences.text: Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.

Our industrial products are used in a diverse set of applications, spanning industrial automation, power generation and distribution systems, medical systems and equipment, defense and aerospace, and vehicle subsystems including those used in electric vehicle powertrain, infotainment and advanced driver assistance systems.

peer_results.rationale: Intel's candidate disclosures focus on the x86 ecosystem strategy and foundry business expansion. While Intel mentions autonomous driving as an emerging field served by its products, the disclosed text lacks specific details on automotive product qualifications, market trends, or technical requirements comparable to MU's specific discussion of automotive memory/storage qualifications and ADAS/infotainment drivers.

comparisons.peer_topic: Automotive Platform Solutions and DRIVE Hyperion Brand
comparisons.peer_summary: The company delivers a complete end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solution for the AV market under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, leveraging AI technology leadership and long-standing automotive relationships. The DRIVE Hyperion platform includes high-performance hardware, a reference sensor set, and an open, modular software platform for autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVIDIA (NVDA) address the automotive market's demand for solutions supporting autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences. MU qualifies specific memory and storage solutions (LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1) for cloud-connected platforms enabling these services, while NVIDIA provides a complete end-to-end platform under the DRIVE Hyperion brand for automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing.

sentences.text: In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.
Automotive market is comprised of platform solutions for automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing.

Leveraging our technology leadership in AI and building on our long-standing automotive relationships, we are delivering a complete end-to-end solution for the AV market under the DRIVE Hyperion brand.

comparisons.peer_summary: High-performance computing technologies are improving advanced driver assistance and automated driving features, with estimates suggesting 39% of new light-duty vehicles sold in 2027 will have Level 2 or higher autonomy.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and Qualcomm (QCOM) discuss the momentum of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and automated driving features in the automotive sector. MU notes that adoption of Level 2+ ADAS capabilities is expanding content per vehicle and driving requirements for high-reliability memory, while QCOM cites industry estimates for the growth of Level 2 or higher autonomy vehicles, driven by high-performance computing technologies.

sentences.text: Adoption of Level 2+ advanced driver-assistance systems capabilities continue to gain momentum, further expanding content per vehicle.

Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

In addition, high-performance, low-power computing technologies, with added security and safety required for automotive products, are being used to improve vehicles with advanced driver assistance and automated driving features that we expect to scale across vehicle tiers and continue the progression toward higher levels of autonomy, safety and convenience.

Analysts estimate that 39% of new light duty vehicles sold globally in 2027 will have Level 2 (i.e., partial driving automation) or higher autonomy, compared to an estimated 20% of new light duty vehicles sold globally in 2024 (TechInsights, September 2024).
